note: Literature notes that absence of selective anterior temporal pole lesions typical of CADASIL distinguishes the recessive form, supporting the premise that temporal involvement in homozygous LoF reflects diffuse changes.

evidence.text: The absence of anterior temporal pole lesions, which are typically found in CADASIL, is regarded as a distinctive feature of the recessive form.

source.title: Novel Mutation of NOTCH3 Gene in a Chinese Patient ... - PMC
source.quote: The absence of anterior temporal pole lesions, which are typically found in CADASIL, is regarded as a distinctive feature of the recessive form.

evidence.text: A homozygous loss-of-function NOTCH3 frameshift variant manifested with early-onset pyramidal signs, epilepsy, and bilateral periventricular confluent white matter hyperintensities distinguishing it from the classical dominant CADASIL presentation.

source.title: A novel homozygous loss-of-function NOTCH3 variant in a Moroccan patient: expanding the spectrum beyond CADASIL
source.quote: Emerging evidence shows that biallelic loss-of-function variants, unlike the gain-of-function variants underlying CADASIL, define a distinct autosomal recessive leukodystrophy characterized by early-onset pyramidal signs, epilepsy, and white matter abnormalities, thereby expanding the phenotypic and molecular spectrum of NOTCH3-related disorders.
